Now summarize concisely. Note the macOS constraint: `fsevents` only installs/builds on darwin; on this Linux box it was skipped and the library fell back to fs.watch. Done. Project scaffolded at `/work`:

- `package.json` — ESM, Node ≥18, `fsevents` as a **darwin-only `optionalDependencies`** entry (native FSEvents binding), plus `start`/`test` scripts.
- `src/watcher.js:110` — `watch()` using native FSEvents (coalesced per-path records, flag decoding) with an `fs.watch` fallback; `src/watcher.js:36` detects the native binding.
- `src/cli.js` — `macos-watch [dir]` prints `event / path / flags`.
- `test/watcher.test.js` — smoke tests; `npm test` passes (3/3).

Important caveat: this box is Linux, so `fsevents` was correctly **skipped** by npm and the code fell back to `fs.watch` (`nativeAvailable() === false`). Run `npm install` on macOS to build/prebuilt-fetch the native module; only then will the low-level FSEvents path activate. If you want a maintained alternative with the same native backend, `@parcel/watcher` is worth considering.
